counterfactual_missing_items: No troponin or serial ECG evidence of acute ischemia
No blood alcohol level or substance screen
No family history or genetic testing for HCM
decisive_items: Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction with systolic anterior motion of mitral valve
response.rationale: C1 is the most complete fixed candidate: it includes the structural HCM/SAM finding and explicitly captures the dynamic LVOT gradient, which explains the syncope. R3 stops at HCM without the dynamic-obstruction complication; R2, R6, R1, and R4 rely on ECG changes, flight/dehydration, or alcohol history and cannot account for the echo findings.

rejected.why: ECG ST/T changes are nonspecific LVH-strain pattern; no troponin or ischemic symptom support and echo shows structural LVOT obstruction.
Normal heart rate and blood pressure plus LVOT obstruction/SAM are not dehydration; flight context is not a sufficient mechanism.
Alcohol blackout does not explain syncope, ECG LVH/strain, or dynamic LVOT obstruction.
Alcohol-related syncope ignores the decisive echocardiographic LVOT gradient and SAM.
